import numpy as np, sys
from PIL import Image
Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS=None

ROOT="/Volumes/Logic Pro/Float Originals Archive/root/"
files=["Deathvalleysky_nps_big.jpeg","Stars_01_(MK).jpeg"]

def band(a, cols):
    return a[:, cols, :].astype(np.float64)

for f in files:
    im = Image.open(ROOT+f).convert("RGB")
    W,H = im.size
    a = np.asarray(im)
    print(f"\n===== {f}  {W}x{H}  ratio {W/H:.4f}")
    # metadata
    print("  exif keys:", list(im.getexif().keys())[:12])
    for k,v in (im.info or {}).items():
        if k in ("jfif","jfif_version","jfif_unit","jfif_density","icc_profile","exif","dpi","progressive","progression","adobe","adobe_transform","photoshop"):
            if k in ("icc_profile","exif","photoshop"): print(f"  info {k}: <{len(v)} bytes>")
            else: print(f"  info {k}: {v}")
        else:
            print(f"  info {k}: {str(v)[:120]}")

    # --- seam test: left edge vs right edge ---
    N=8
    L = band(a, list(range(0,N)))              # leftmost N cols
    R = band(a, list(range(W-N,W)))            # rightmost N cols
    # wrap match: right edge should continue into left edge
    d_wrap = np.abs(R.mean(axis=1) - L.mean(axis=1)).mean()
    # baseline: compare left edge to a random interior column band, same distance apart isn't defined,
    # so use mean |diff| between two ADJACENT interior columns (best case) and two far-apart bands (worst case)
    mid = W//2
    d_adj  = np.abs(a[:,mid,:].astype(float) - a[:,mid+1,:].astype(float)).mean()
    d_far  = np.abs(band(a,list(range(mid-N,mid))).mean(axis=1) - band(a,list(range(mid,mid+N))).mean(axis=1)).mean()
    # random unrelated pair
    rng=np.random.default_rng(7)
    ds=[]
    for _ in range(200):
        i,j = rng.integers(N, W-N, 2)
        ds.append(np.abs(a[:,i,:].astype(float)-a[:,j,:].astype(float)).mean())
    d_rand=np.mean(ds)
    print(f"  wrap seam L<->R  : {d_wrap:7.3f}")
    print(f"  adjacent interior: {d_adj:7.3f}   (perfect-continuity reference)")
    print(f"  8px-apart interior:{d_far:7.3f}")
    print(f"  random col pair  : {d_rand:7.3f}   (no-relationship reference)")
    verdict = "WRAPS (360)" if d_wrap < d_far*1.6 else ("does NOT wrap" if d_wrap > d_rand*0.5 else "ambiguous")
    print(f"  --> {verdict}")

    # --- pole test: are top/bottom rows constant per-row (equirect pole squash)? ---
    for name,row in (("top row",a[0]),("bottom row",a[-1]),("row 5%",a[int(H*0.05)]),("row 95%",a[int(H*0.95)])):
        print(f"  {name:9s} horiz std: {row.astype(float).std(axis=0).mean():7.3f}")
PY

content.text: Both are wide night panoramas. Now the decisive geometry test — star shapes elongate *horizontally* toward the poles in equirect and *vertically* in cylindrical, by the same factor, so measuring star aspect vs row identifies the projection.

input.command:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rashford-Library-Mobile-Documents-com-apple-CloudDocs-Developer-Float/8d423303-d0e9-4b2d-83f4-d37bffea1d7d/scratchpad && cat > stars.py <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter
Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS=None
ROOT="/Volumes/Logic Pro/Float Originals Archive/root/"

def measure(path, sky_top, sky_bot, label):
    im = Image.open(ROOT+path).convert("L")
    W,H = im.size
    a = np.asarray(im).astype(np.float32)
    bg = np.asarray(im.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(12))).astype(np.float32)
    d = a - bg
    noise = np.median(np.abs(d - np.median(d)))*1.4826
    thr = 6.0*noise
    print(f"\n===== {label}  {W}x{H}   noise sigma {noise:.3f}  thr {thr:.2f}")

    # local maxima
    R=1
    ismax = np.ones_like(d, bool)
    for dy in (-1,0,1):
        for dx in (-1,0,1):
            if dy==0 and dx==0: continue
            ismax &= d >= np.roll(np.roll(d,dy,0),dx,1)
    cand = ismax & (d>thr) & (a<252)      # drop saturated
    cand[:sky_top]=False; cand[sky_bot:]=False
    cand[:, :6]=False; cand[:, -6:]=False
    ys,xs = np.nonzero(cand)
    print(f"  raw peaks in sky band rows {sky_top}-{sky_bot}: {len(ys)}")

    W_=5   # half-window
    rows=[]; ratios=[]; sx_l=[]; sy_l=[]
    yy,xx = np.mgrid[-W_:W_+1, -W_:W_+1]
    for y,x in zip(ys,xs):
        if y<W_ or y>=H-W_ or x<W_ or x>=W-W_: continue
        p = d[y-W_:y+W_+1, x-W_:x+W_+1].copy()
        # isolation: no other comparable peak in window
        if p.max()!=p[W_,W_]: continue
        p[p<0]=0
        s=p.sum()
        if s<=0: continue
        cx=(p*xx).sum()/s; cy=(p*yy).sum()/s

content.text:
Both checked. Summary:

## `Deathvalleysky_nps_big.jpeg` — genuinely 360° ✅
- **4000 × 1290** (ratio 3.10), Racetrack Playa, EXIF date 2007-10-30.
- **Wrap confirmed.** Left/right edge difference is 7.44 vs 6.12 for two *adjacent interior* columns and 22.8 for an unrelated column pair — i.e. the seam is as continuous as ordinary neighbouring pixels. Rolling it 180° puts the former edges in the middle of `seam_deathvalley.jpg`, and terrain, playa cracks, clouds and stars all run straight through (there's a faint hairline on the ridge, nothing more).
- **It is pure monochrome** — saturation is exactly 0.0000 across every pixel, R=G=B. Not a desaturated-looking colour image; there is no colour to recover. Worth knowing before it goes anywhere near a colour library.
- **Not a full sphere vertically.** Horizon sits at row 936 of 1290 (72.6% down), so 936 px of sky vs 354 px of ground — asymmetric, and both zenith and nadir are missing. So it's a grounded scene needing cap outpaint, same shape of job as Bontecou.

## `Stars_01_(MK).jpeg` — not 360 ❌
Your first glance was right, and the file says so itself. EXIF `UserComment`:

```
Projection: Cylindrical (1)
FOV: 334 x 144
```

A Hugin stitch — cylindrical, not equirect, and 334° not 360°. **Wrap test agrees:** edge difference 43.1, *worse* than the 32.3 random-column baseline, against 7.1 for adjacent interior columns. The rolled image shows why: one end is warm light-pollution glow over a distant low treeline, the other is cool blue sky with a near, tall treeline.

Caveat on those FOV numbers — 6070 × 2000 doesn't correspond to 334° × 144° in cylindrical projection under any consistent scale, so the delivered JPEG is a **crop** of that stitch project and neither figure describes the file. The true coverage still needs solving.

Provenance, since you didn't know: Sony SLT-A77V, 2014-06-18, Lightroom 5.3, GPS 52°27'N 12°29'E — **Havelsee, Brandenburg, Germany**. Spotlight also found a copy at `Dropbox/Photos/Wallpaper/Picture of the Day/Stars_01_(MK).jpg`, so it came out of your wallpaper collection rather than a sourced archive — there's no licence trail on it. The `(MK)` suffix is a Wikimedia uploader-initials convention, so it's probably traceable there, but I'd want that confirmed before it ships.

## One correction
I also tried identifying Death Valley's projection from star-shape anisotropy vs row, and it produced a clean-looking trend. It's not valid — any cylindrical-family projection must stretch stars *horizontally* by sec φ, and measured `sigma_x` is flat in both files, so what I measured was lens astigmatism and star trailing, not projection. Death Valley's equirect-vs-cylindrical question is still open; the seam and metadata results above don't depend on it.

Both files are read-only reconnaissance so far — I haven't changed anything in the repo or touched the pipeline.

New section **"Grounded candidates — sources, not yet rendered"** (2 cards), inserted after the Planets block between `<!-- CANDIDATES:START/END -->` markers so it's scriptable later. Thumbnails at 1024px wide in `triage_originals/cand_*.jpg` (~70 KB each).

One thing I had to change: the default `.card img` rule crops to 2/1 with `object-fit:cover`, which on a 3.1:1 panorama would have hidden the left/right edges — exactly what needs judging. Added a `.pano` class (true aspect, no crop, no height cap) scoped to the new section, so nothing else on the page is affected. Both cards pick up the REMOVE and Premium toggles automatically. 57 cards, tags balanced, no missing images.

Only one lake image exists in the archive (`Bontecou_Lake_Milky_Way_panorama.jpeg`), so I added that one — say the word if "the lake ones" meant others somewhere else. Seam 20.5 vs 4.87 for adjacent columns — a real gap, but well short of the 26.5 random baseline, consistent with the 350° figure.

## Death Valley in colour: it doesn't exist, and it can't
Not just "I couldn't find one" — the reason is structural:

- The image is **Dan Duriscoe, NPS, 2005**, public domain, published via [APOD 2007-05-08](https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/ap070508.html).
- It's an **NPS night-sky-monitoring mosaic** — 30 frames through a **V-band photometric filter on a research-grade monochrome CCD**. That's a light-pollution measuring instrument: single passband, one channel. The colour was never captured.
- All three [Commons variants](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deathvalleysky_nps_big.jpg) (`big`, `edit`, `polar`) measure **max** saturation 0.00000 — I downloaded and checked rather than inferring, because the page-fetch guessed "colour" from the filenames and was wrong.
- The only 360° night panorama of Racetrack Playa in [that Commons category](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Racetrack_Playa) is this one. The other panoramas there are daytime/sunrise. Rogelio Bernal Andreo has a colour Racetrack Playa + Milky Way shot, but it's copyrighted and not 360.

So colour would have to be **invented** — diffusion colourisation, the same class of tool the pipeline already runs for outpaint. That's a real option, just be clear it's fabrication, not recovery.

Two incidental finds worth knowing:

- **Your file is 1290px tall; the Commons original is 1288.** Not the same file, and I don't know where the extra 2px came from.
- The APOD wording — "full-sky … increasingly stretched at high altitudes to make it rectangular" — reads as equirect with the top edge near the zenith, and horizon row 936 at 4000px/360° puts the top edge at +84°, which fits. But stars near the top show none of the ~9× horizontal smear equirect at +84° demands. The two lines of evidence conflict, so I've recorded the projection as still unsolved rather than picking one. 1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Plain-model neural SR on the ai/comfyui V100, for equirect sources below target res.
3	
4	Rick's standing rule: sources below target are ALWAYS upscaled by neural inference —
5	there is no "never upscale past the source" (that uninvited cap caused the grainy
6	SPHEREx scenes). Model choice is whatever gives the best result; for equirect
7	starfield/all-sky sources that is RealESRGAN_x4plus by A/B (2026-07-24, vs NMKD-Siax /
8	UltraSharp / UltimateSDUpscale): faithful color on diffuse nebulosity (USDU shifts
9	hue + speckles), round clean stars (Siax/UltraSharp turn survey noise into worm
10	artifacts), no tile seams, and ~100x faster than diffusion. The USDU diffusion recipe
11	remains the choice for flat POTM masters (master_sr.py, device-approved parity).
12	
13	Equirects are wrap-padded before SR so the lon +/-180 seam (directly behind the
14	viewer) stays continuous, then cropped back after the model pass. Downscaling to the
15	exact target after the 4x model pass is Lanczos — the rule governs upscaling only.
16	
17	The workflow is mirrored in the ComfyUI web UI as "equirect_realesrgan_sr" for study.
18	"""
19	import json
20	import os
21	import subprocess
22	import tempfile
23	import time
24	
25	from PIL import Image
26	
27	Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
28	NS = "ai"
29	MODEL = "RealESRGAN_x4plus.pth"
30	MODEL_SCALE = 4
31	WRAP_PAD = 64                       # px of left/right wrap context fed to the model
32	
33	
34	def _log(msg):
35	    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)
36	
37	
38	def comfy_pod():
39	    out = subprocess.run(
40	        ["kubectl", "get", "pods", "-n", NS, "-l", "app=comfyui", "--no-headers",
41	         "-o", "custom-columns=:metadata.name"], capture_output=True, text=True)
42	    pod = out.stdout.strip().split("\n")[0]
43	    if not pod:
44	        raise RuntimeError("no comfyui pod found (is Ollama holding the GPU? check replicas)")
45	    return pod
46	
47	
48	def _workflow(input_filename, out_prefix):
49	    return {
50	        "1": {"class_type": "LoadImage", "inputs": {"image": input_filename}},
51	        "2": {"class_type": "UpscaleModelLoader", "inputs": {"model_name": MODEL}},
52	        "3": {"class_type": "ImageUpscaleWithModel",
53	              "inputs": {"upscale_model": ["2", 0], "image": ["1", 0]}},
54	        "4": {"class_type": "SaveImage",
55	              "inputs": {"filename_prefix": out_prefix, "images": ["3", 0]}},
56	    }
57	
58	
59	def _run_pod(pod, local_png, tag, out_png, timeout_s=1800):
60	    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", local_png, f"{NS}/{pod}:/basedir/input/nsr_{tag}.png"],
61	                   check=True)
62	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as tf:
63	        json.dump({"prompt": _workflow(f"nsr_{tag}.png", f"nsrout_{tag}")}, tf)
64	        wfp = tf.name
65	    try:
66	        subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", wfp, f"{NS}/{pod}:/tmp/nsr_{tag}.json"], check=True)
67	    finally:
68	        os.unlink(wfp)
69	    before = {l.strip() for l in subprocess.run(
70	        ["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
71	         f"ls /basedir/output/nsrout_{tag}_*.png 2>/dev/null"],
72	        capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()}
73	    r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
74	                        f"curl -s -m 15 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt "
75	                        f"-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/nsr_{tag}.json"],
76	                       capture_output=True, text=True)
77	    if '"prompt_id"' not in r.stdout:
78	        raise RuntimeError(f"SR submit failed for {tag}: {r.stdout[:300]} {r.stderr[:200]}")
79	    # Wait for a NEW file under this tag rather than for the queue to read idle. The
80	    # queue can report empty before ComfyUI registers a just-POSTed prompt, and the old
81	    # code then took `ls -t | head -1` — the PREVIOUS run's upscale for this exact tag,
82	    # silently, in about a second. Third instance of this pattern (see sky360._run and
83	    # process_backdrops.depth_via_comfy); this is the worst-placed of the three because
84	    # sr_equirect runs on EVERY scene and the tags (`<scene>_sky_p0`) accumulate output
85	    # files across every previous render, so there is always a stale file ready to be
86	    # picked up. Requiring an unseen filename makes that impossible rather than unlikely.
87	    def listing():
88	        r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
89	                            f"ls /basedir/output/nsrout_{tag}_*.png 2>/dev/null"],
90	                           capture_output=True, text=True)
91	        return {l.strip() for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()}
92	
93	    t0 = time.time()
94	    remote = ""
95	    while time.time() - t0 < timeout_s:
96	        time.sleep(4)
97	        fresh = sorted(listing() - before)
98	        if fresh:
99	            remote = fresh[-1]
100	            q = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
101	                                "curl -s -m 6 http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue"],
102	                               capture_output=True, text=True)
103	            try:
104	                d = json.loads(q.stdout)
105	                if len(d.get("queue_running", [])) + len(d.get("queue_pending", [])) == 0:
106	                    break
107	            except Exception:
108	                break
109	    if not remote:
110	        raise RuntimeError(f"no NEW SR output for {tag} after {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
111	    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", f"{NS}/{pod}:{remote}", out_png], check=True)
112	
113	
114	def _sr_pass(im, tag):
115	    """One wrap-padded RealESRGAN x4 pass over a PIL equirect. Returns a PIL Image."""
116	    import numpy as np
117	    arr = np.asarray(im.convert("RGB"))
118	    padded = np.concatenate([arr[:, -WRAP_PAD:], arr, arr[:, :WRAP_PAD]], axis=1)
119	    pod = comfy_pod()
120	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
121	        src = os.path.join(td, "in.png")
122	        out = os.path.join(td, "out.png")
123	        Image.fromarray(padded, "RGB").save(src)
124	        t0 = time.time()
125	        _run_pod(pod, src, tag, out)
126	        up = Image.open(out).convert("RGB")
127	        _log(f"  SR {tag}: {im.size[0]}x{im.size[1]} -> {up.size[0]}x{up.size[1]} "
128	             f"({MODEL}, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
129	        pad = WRAP_PAD * MODEL_SCALE
130	        return up.crop((pad, 0, up.size[0] - pad, up.size[1]))
131	
132	
133	def sr_equirect(im, tag, target_w):
134	    """Upscale a PIL equirect to exactly (target_w, target_w//2), wrap-padded across the
135	    lon seam so +/-180 (directly behind the viewer) stays continuous.
136	
137	    Multi-pass when one x4 undershoots: the sky360 diffusion canvas is 1536 wide and the
138	    target is 12288, so it needs x8. Between passes the frame is Lanczos-shrunk to
139	    target/4 so the FINAL x4 lands exactly on target — otherwise the last pass would have
140	    to produce (and kubectl cp) a 300-megapixel intermediate. Sources that already reach
141	    target/4 in one pass behave exactly as before (single pass, then Lanczos down)."""
142	    n = 0
143	    while im.width * MODEL_SCALE < target_w:
144	        im = _sr_pass(im, f"{tag}_p{n}")
145	        n += 1
146	        if im.width * MODEL_SCALE > target_w:      # another full pass would overshoot
147	            im = im.resize((target_w // MODEL_SCALE, target_w // (2 * MODEL_SCALE)),
148	                           Image.LANCZOS)
149	    up = _sr_pass(im, f"{tag}_p{n}" if n else tag)
150	    if up.size != (target_w, target_w // 2):
151	        up = up.resize((target_w, target_w // 2), Image.LANCZOS)
152	    return up

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Colorize the Death Valley mono 360 pano — CHROMA ONLY.

The source (Dan Duriscoe / NPS, 2005) is a V-band photometric mosaic off a monochrome
science CCD: saturation is exactly 0.00000 on every pixel of all three Commons variants.
There is no colour to recover, so any colour here is INVENTED. Say so in CREDITS.

Method, and why it is this way:

  Diffusion supplies chroma; the original supplies luminance. Full stop. The mono
  luminance IS the photometry and IS all the detail (stars, playa cracks, ridgelines),
  so letting a sampler touch it would trade real data for plausible mush. Working in
  YCbCr and keeping Y from the source means:
    - every star, crack and ridge is bit-preserved in luma
    - the 360 wrap stays continuous in luma BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck
    - tone/exposure cannot drift, so nothing downstream needs re-grading
  Chroma is low-frequency, so it is generated at 1536 wide and Lanczos-upsampled to
  4000. That also dodges tiling entirely — no USDU, no seam-fix pass, no tile grid.

  Wrap-padding before the sampler (same trick as neural_sr.sr_equirect) keeps the
  lon +/-180 seam from getting two different hues.

Candidates: three denoise levels plus an analytic control that uses no diffusion at
all, so there is something honest to compare against.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None

NS = "ai"
CKPT = "realisticVisionV60B1_v51VAE.safetensors"
SRC = "/Volumes/Logic Pro/Float Originals Archive/root/Deathvalleysky_nps_big.jpeg"
OUT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

WORK_W = 1536                 # chroma is low-frequency; this is plenty
WRAP_PAD = 192                # px of wrap context at work scale
HORIZON = 936                 # measured: sharpest sky->playa step, row 936 of 1290
STEPS = 28
CFG = 7.0

# "monochrome / black and white / grayscale" in the NEGATIVE is the whole trick for a
# mono init — without it the sampler happily agrees the picture is already fine.
PROMPT = ("color night photograph, Milky Way arch over a dry lake bed, deep blue "
          "night sky, warm golden galactic core, faint green airglow low on the "
          "horizon, pale tan cracked mud playa, dark silhouetted desert mountains, "
          "natural night colors, astrophotography, rich color")
NEG = ("monochrome, black and white, grayscale, desaturated, colorless, sepia, "
       "text, watermark, signature, caption, border, frame, vignette, "
       "oversaturated, neon, magenta cast, purple cast, rainbow, "
       "blurry, lowres, jpeg artifacts, daylight, sunset, city lights, aurora")


def _log(m):
    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {m}", flush=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BT.601 in float
def to_ycbcr(rgb):
    r, g, b = rgb[..., 0], rgb[..., 1], rgb[..., 2]
    y = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b
    cb = -0.168736 * r - 0.331264 * g + 0.5 * b + 0.5
    cr = 0.5 * r - 0.418688 * g - 0.081312 * b + 0.5
    return y, cb, cr


def to_rgb(y, cb, cr):
    cb = cb - 0.5
    cr = cr - 0.5
    r = y + 1.402 * cr
    g = y - 0.344136 * cb - 0.714136 * cr
    b = y + 1.772 * cb
    return np.clip(np.stack([r, g, b], axis=-1), 0.0, 1.0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- ComfyUI on sdf1
def comfy_pod():
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["kubectl", "get", "pods", "-n", NS, "-l", "app=comfyui", "--no-headers",
         "-o", "custom-columns=:metadata.name"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    pod = out.stdout.strip().split("\n")[0]
    if not pod:
        raise RuntimeError("no comfyui pod (is Ollama holding the GPU? check replicas)")
    return pod


def img2img_wf(name, prompt, neg, seed, denoise, out_prefix):
    return {
        "1": {"class_type": "LoadImage", "inputs": {"image": name}},
        "2": {"class_type": "CheckpointLoaderSimple", "inputs": {"ckpt_name": CKPT}},
        "3": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode", "inputs": {"clip": ["2", 1], "text": prompt}},
        "4": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode", "inputs": {"clip": ["2", 1], "text": neg}},
        "5": {"class_type": "VAEEncode", "inputs": {"pixels": ["1", 0], "vae": ["2", 2]}},
        "6": {"class_type": "KSampler",
              "inputs": {"model": ["2", 0], "positive": ["3", 0], "negative": ["4", 0],
                         "latent_image": ["5", 0], "seed": seed, "steps": STEPS,
                         "cfg": CFG, "sampler_name": "dpmpp_2m",
                         "scheduler": "karras", "denoise": denoise}},
        "7": {"class_type": "VAEDecode", "inputs": {"samples": ["6", 0], "vae": ["2", 2]}},
        "8": {"class_type": "SaveImage",
              "inputs": {"filename_prefix": out_prefix, "images": ["7", 0]}},
    }


def run_pod(pod, local_png, tag, wf, out_png, timeout_s=1800):
    """Submit and wait for an UNSEEN output filename — never `ls -t | head -1`, which
    silently returns a previous run's image for the same tag (see the long comment in
    neural_sr._run_pod; this is the fourth site of that bug)."""
    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", local_png, f"{NS}/{pod}:/basedir/input/{tag}.png"],
                   check=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as tf:
        json.dump({"prompt": wf}, tf)
        wfp = tf.name
    try:
        subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", wfp, f"{NS}/{pod}:/tmp/{tag}.json"], check=True)
    finally:
        os.unlink(wfp)

    def listing():
        r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
                            f"ls /basedir/output/{tag}out_*.png 2>/dev/null"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        return {l.strip() for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()}

    before = listing()
    r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
                        f"curl -s -m 20 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt "
                        f"-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/{tag}.json"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    if '"prompt_id"' not in r.stdout:
        raise RuntimeError(f"submit failed {tag}: {r.stdout[:400]} {r.stderr[:200]}")

    t0 = time.time()
    remote = ""
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout_s:
        time.sleep(4)
        fresh = sorted(listing() - before)
        if fresh:
            remote = fresh[-1]
            q = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
                                "curl -s -m 6 http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue"],
                               capture_output=True, text=True)
            try:
                d = json.loads(q.stdout)
                if len(d.get("queue_running", [])) + len(d.get("queue_pending", [])) == 0:
                    break
            except Exception:
                break
    if not remote:
        raise RuntimeError(f"no NEW output for {tag} after {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", f"{NS}/{pod}:{remote}", out_png], check=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- chroma recombine
def recombine(mono_full, cb_small, cr_small, sat=1.0, chroma_blur=0):
    """Original full-res luma + upsampled generated chroma."""
    H, W = mono_full.shape
    def up(c):
        im = Image.fromarray(np.clip(c * 255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8), "L")
        if chroma_blur:
            im = im.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(chroma_blur))
        return np.asarray(im.resize((W, H), Image.LANCZOS)).astype(np.float64) / 255.0
    cb = (up(cb_small) - 0.5) * sat + 0.5
    cr = (up(cr_small) - 0.5) * sat + 0.5
    return to_rgb(mono_full, cb, cr)


def analytic(mono_full):
    """No diffusion. A hand-authored night grade: sky gets a deep-blue -> warm-core
    ramp keyed on luminance, ground gets a neutral-warm tan, and a soft airglow band
    sits just above the horizon. This exists so there is a control — if diffusion
    cannot beat a 30-line ramp, it is not earning its place."""
    H, W = mono_full.shape
    y = mono_full
    # Luminance-keyed sky ramp: dark sky deep blue, bright MW core warm gold.
    # Stops are (luma, r, g, b) as multipliers around neutral.
    stops = np.array([
        [0.00, 0.62, 0.74, 1.00],   # darkest sky: cold blue
        [0.12, 0.72, 0.82, 1.00],
        [0.26, 0.95, 0.93, 1.00],   # MW mid: near neutral
        [0.45, 1.08, 1.00, 0.90],   # MW core: warm
        [1.00, 1.10, 1.02, 0.92],
    ])
    rr = np.interp(y, stops[:, 0], stops[:, 1])
    gg = np.interp(y, stops[:, 0], stops[:, 2])
    bb = np.interp(y, stops[:, 0], stops[:, 3])
    sky = np.stack([y * rr, y * gg, y * bb], axis=-1)
    # Ground: neutral, faintly warm tan.
    gnd = np.stack([y * 1.04, y * 1.00, y * 0.93], axis=-1)
    rows = np.arange(H)[:, None, None]
    blend = np.clip((rows - (HORIZON - 25)) / 50.0, 0, 1)   # soft horizon crossfade
    out = sky * (1 - blend) + gnd * blend
    # Airglow: a warm/green band hugging the horizon from above.
    d = np.clip(1.0 - np.abs(rows - HORIZON) / 260.0, 0, 1) ** 2 * (rows < HORIZON)
    out[..., 0] += 0.030 * d[..., 0] * y
    out[..., 1] += 0.040 * d[..., 0] * y
    out[..., 2] -= 0.012 * d[..., 0] * y
    return np.clip(out, 0, 1)


def main():
    _log(f"source: {SRC}")
    mono = Image.open(SRC).convert("L")
    W, H = mono.size
    m = np.asarray(mono).astype(np.float64) / 255.0
    _log(f"mono {W}x{H}  (luma preserved bit-for-bit; only chroma is generated)")

    work_h = int(round(WORK_W * H / W / 8)) * 8
    small = mono.convert("RGB").resize((WORK_W, work_h), Image.LANCZOS)
    a = np.asarray(small)
    padded = np.concatenate([a[:, -WRAP_PAD:], a, a[:, :WRAP_PAD]], axis=1)
    _log(f"work canvas {padded.shape[1]}x{padded.shape[0]} (incl {WRAP_PAD}px wrap pad)")

    pod = comfy_pod()
    _log(f"pod {pod}")

    results = {}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        src_png = os.path.join(td, "in.png")
        Image.fromarray(padded, "RGB").save(src_png)
        for dn in (0.35, 0.50, 0.65):
            tag = f"dvcol{int(dn * 100)}"
            out_png = os.path.join(td, f"{tag}.png")
            wf = img2img_wf(f"{tag}.png", PROMPT, NEG, 12345, dn, f"{tag}out")
            t0 = time.time()
            try:
                run_pod(pod, src_png, tag, wf, out_png)
            except Exception as e:
                _log(f"  denoise {dn}: FAILED — {e}")
                continue
            gen = np.asarray(Image.open(out_png).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float64) / 255.0
            gen = gen[:, WRAP_PAD:gen.shape[1] - WRAP_PAD]        # drop wrap pad
            _, cb, cr = to_ycbcr(gen)
            csat = float(np.sqrt((cb - 0.5) ** 2 + (cr - 0.5) ** 2).mean())
            _log(f"  denoise {dn}: {time.time() - t0:.0f}s  mean chroma radius {csat:.4f}")
            rgb = recombine(m, cb, cr, sat=1.0, chroma_blur=2)
            p = os.path.join(OUT, f"dv_color_dn{int(dn * 100)}.jpg")
            Image.fromarray((rgb * 255).round().astype(np.uint8), "RGB").save(p, quality=94)
            results[f"dn{int(dn*100)}"] = p
            _log(f"  -> {os.path.basename(p)}")

    p = os.path.join(OUT, "dv_color_analytic.jpg")
    Image.fromarray((analytic(m) * 255).round().astype(np.uint8), "RGB").save(p, quality=94)
    results["analytic"] = p
    _log(f"analytic control -> {os.path.basename(p)}")

    p = os.path.join(OUT, "dv_mono_ref.jpg")
    mono.convert("RGB").save(p, quality=94)
    results["mono"] = p

    # Report measured saturation of each candidate, and confirm luma is untouched.
    _log("=== measured ===")
    for k, path in results.items():
        a = np.asarray(Image.open(path).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float64) / 255.0
        mx, mn = a.max(axis=2), a.min(axis=2)
        sat = np.where(mx > 0, (mx - mn) / np.maximum(mx, 1e-9), 0)
        y, _, _ = to_ycbcr(a)
        dl = np.abs(y - m).mean() * 255
        _log(f"  {k:9s} mean_sat {sat.mean():.4f}  p99 {np.percentile(sat,99):.4f}  "
             f"luma drift {dl:.2f}/255")
    json.dump({k: os.path.basename(v) for k, v in results.items()},
              open(os.path.join(OUT, "dv_candidates.json"), "w"), indent=1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

incoherent. So low-pass the chroma hard and rescale it. Luma is still the untouched
original, so nothing here can damage detail.

The blur MUST wrap horizontally or the 360 seam gets a colour step. That is the one

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
HORIZON = 936


def ycbcr(rgb):
    r, g, b = rgb[..., 0], rgb[..., 1], rgb[..., 2]
    return (0.299*r + 0.587*g + 0.114*b,
            -0.168736*r - 0.331264*g + 0.5*b + 0.5,
            0.5*r - 0.418688*g - 0.081312*b + 0.5)


def to_rgb(y, cb, cr):
    cb, cr = cb - 0.5, cr - 0.5
    return np.clip(np.stack([y + 1.402*cr,
                             y - 0.344136*cb - 0.714136*cr,
                             y + 1.772*cb], -1), 0, 1)


def wrap_blur(c, radius):
    """Gaussian blur that wraps in x — otherwise the lon +/-180 seam gets a colour step."""
    if radius <= 0:
        return c
    pad = int(radius * 3)
    H, W = c.shape
    ext = np.concatenate([c[:, -pad:], c, c[:, :pad]], axis=1)
    im = Image.fromarray(np.clip(ext*255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8), "L")
    im = im.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(radius))
    return np.asarray(im).astype(np.float64)[:, pad:pad+W] / 255.0

    _, cb, cr = ycbcr(a)
    src[tag] = (cb, cr)

    cb = (cb - 0.5)*sat + 0.5
    cr = (cr - 0.5)*sat + 0.5
    out = to_rgb(mono, cb, cr)

    mx, mn = out.max(2), out.min(2)
    s = np.where(mx > 0, (mx-mn)/np.maximum(mx, 1e-9), 0)
    y, _, _ = ycbcr(out)
    print(f"  {name:34s} mean_sat {s.mean():.4f}  luma drift {np.abs(y-mono).mean()*255:.2f}/255")

print("=== smoothed variants ===")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Composite the alpha planet renders over the deep_star_map, one yaw per body.

Why a separate script: the Cycles render is the expensive part and the star-map framing is
the cheap part, so they are decoupled. Re-run this alone to change a yaw or swap the
backdrop; `render_planets.py --preview` only has to run when a body itself changes.

Why gnomonic and not a crop: the star map is an EQUIRECT. Pasting a rectangular crop of it
behind a perspective camera stretches longitudes near the frame edges and squashes them at
centre — on a dense star field that reads as a subtly warped sky. So the background is
properly reprojected: for every output pixel, build the camera ray, convert to (lon, lat),
sample the equirect. The camera's real lens/sensor/resolution come from the .cam.json
sidecar `render_preview` writes, so this cannot drift from what Blender actually rendered.

Run:  python3 scripts/composite_planet_previews.py            # all bodies found
      python3 scripts/composite_planet_previews.py --only saturn
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
PREV = os.path.join(REPO, "upscale", "planet_prev")
STARMAP = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/_sr_cache",
                       "starmap_2020_8k_12288.png")
STARMAP_FALLBACK = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw", "starmap_2020_8k.exr")

# Per-body yaw into the star map, degrees. Spread around the sphere so no two cards show the
# same starfield — Rick asked for the starting viewpoint varied horizontally. Values are
# arbitrary but FIXED: keeping them stable means a re-render changes the body and not the
# background, so the two are separately judgeable.
YAW = {
    "saturn":       0.0,
    "saturn_baked": 72.0,
    "jupiter":      144.0,
    "iapetus":      216.0,
    "venus":        288.0,
}
# A dim backdrop: the star map at full strength competes with the body and the card stops
# being about the body. This is a display choice for the contact sheet only.
BG_GAIN = 0.55


def load_starmap():
    p = STARMAP if os.path.exists(STARMAP) else STARMAP_FALLBACK
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        sys.exit(f"no star map found at {STARMAP} or {STARMAP_FALLBACK}")
    im = Image.open(p).convert("RGB")
    print(f"star map: {os.path.basename(p)} {im.size[0]}x{im.size[1]}")
    return np.asarray(im).astype(np.float32) / 255.0


def gnomonic(eq, out_w, out_h, hfov_deg, yaw_deg, pitch_deg=0.0):
    """Rectilinear view of an equirect. Returns float RGB in [0,1]."""
    H, W = eq.shape[:2]
    hfov = np.radians(hfov_deg)
    f = (out_w * 0.5) / np.tan(hfov * 0.5)          # focal length in pixels

    xs = np.arange(out_w, dtype=np.float64) - (out_w - 1) * 0.5
    ys = np.arange(out_h, dtype=np.float64) - (out_h - 1) * 0.5
    xx, yy = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)

    # Camera ray: +Z forward, +X right, +Y up (y flipped because rows increase downward).
    dx, dy, dz = xx, -yy, np.full_like(xx, f)
    n = np.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz)
    dx, dy, dz = dx/n, dy/n, dz/n

    # Pitch about X, then yaw about Y.
    p = np.radians(pitch_deg)
    dy2 = dy*np.cos(p) - dz*np.sin(p)
    dz2 = dy*np.sin(p) + dz*np.cos(p)
    a = np.radians(yaw_deg)
    dx3 = dx*np.cos(a) + dz2*np.sin(a)
    dz3 = -dx*np.sin(a) + dz2*np.cos(a)

    lon = np.arctan2(dx3, dz3)                       # -pi..pi
    lat = np.arcsin(np.clip(dy2, -1, 1))             # -pi/2..pi/2

    u = (lon / (2*np.pi) + 0.5) * W
    v = (0.5 - lat / np.pi) * H

    # Bilinear, wrapping in longitude and clamping in latitude.
    u0 = np.floor(u).astype(np.int64)
    v0 = np.floor(v).astype(np.int64)
    fu, fv = u - u0, v - v0
    u0m, u1m = u0 % W, (u0 + 1) % W
    v0m = np.clip(v0, 0, H-1)
    v1m = np.clip(v0 + 1, 0, H-1)
    out = np.empty((out_h, out_w, 3), np.float32)
    for c in range(3):
        ch = eq[..., c]
        top = ch[v0m, u0m]*(1-fu) + ch[v0m, u1m]*fu
        bot = ch[v1m, u0m]*(1-fu) + ch[v1m, u1m]*fu
        out[..., c] = top*(1-fv) + bot*fv
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only")
    ap.add_argument("--gain", type=float, default=BG_GAIN)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    names = [args.only] if args.only else sorted(YAW)
    todo = [(n, os.path.join(PREV, f"{n}.png")) for n in names]
    todo = [(n, p) for n, p in todo if os.path.exists(p)]
    if not todo:
        sys.exit(f"no RGBA renders in {PREV} — run render_planets.py --preview first")

    eq = load_starmap()
    for name, png in todo:
        fg = np.asarray(Image.open(png).convert("RGBA")).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        h, w = fg.shape[:2]
        cam = os.path.join(PREV, f"{name}.cam.json")
        if os.path.exists(cam):
            meta = json.load(open(cam))
            hfov = meta["hfov_deg"]
            # Blender's AUTO sensor fit applies the sensor to the LARGER dimension, so when
            # the render is wider than tall the stored hfov is already the horizontal one.
            if meta["resolution"][1] > meta["resolution"][0]:
                hfov = np.degrees(2*np.arctan(np.tan(np.radians(hfov)/2) *
                                              meta["resolution"][0]/meta["resolution"][1]))
        else:
            hfov = 39.60          # Blender default 50mm on a 36mm sensor
            print(f"  {name}: no .cam.json, assuming hfov {hfov} deg")

        bg = gnomonic(eq, w, h, hfov, YAW[name]) * args.gain
        a = fg[..., 3:4]
        comp = fg[..., :3]*a + bg*(1-a)
        out = os.path.join(PREV, f"{name}.jpg")
        Image.fromarray((np.clip(comp, 0, 1)*255).round().astype(np.uint8), "RGB").save(
            out, quality=92)
        cover = float(a.mean())
        print(f"  {name:13s} yaw {YAW[name]:5.1f} deg  hfov {hfov:.2f}  "
              f"body covers {cover*100:.1f}% -> {os.path.basename(out)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.text:
Here's where everything stands while the Saturn bake finishes.

**Death Valley colourisation — done.** dn0.50, blue plume removed. Full-res colour master at `upscale/dv_colorized_dn50.jpg`. Method: diffusion supplied *only* chroma, your original mono supplied luminance — measured luma drift **0.000/255**, so every star, playa crack and ridgeline is still the real photometric data. The blotch fix blends toward the surrounding playa's own chroma, dropping blue excess from +0.096 to +0.006. Saturation 0.168, essentially the 0.166 of Bontecou, a real colour night pano. The card says plainly that the colour is invented, since it is.

**Saturn's rings — two separate bugs, both found.** The USDZ was never at fault (`doubleSided = 1`, opacity correctly wired to the texture's alpha):
1. **Live-lit Saturn:** the ring normal is (0.449, 0, 0.893) and the app's key light was (−0.815, 0.367, 0.448) — **N·L = +0.034**, i.e. lit at 88° grazing, ~3% brightness, black against a black sky. Your requested sun direction fixes this outright: **N·L = +0.99**.
2. **Baked Saturn:** the ring annulus is a separate, un-baked, ordinary diffuse material, and the body was flagged `unlit` so it received *no light at all*. The sun fix alone would not have touched this. The `unlit` guard turned out to be unnecessary — the baked globe has `diffuseColor = (0,0,0)`, so it cannot show a second terminator. Every body now gets the sun. Simulator build: **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.

One consequence you should know: with the sun behind the viewer, Saturn's ring shadow falls *behind* the rings, so the bake's whole feature stops being visible — the two Saturn cards will look alike again, for a new reason. The bake itself is intact; it's just not visible from this angle. Your call whether that's worth revisiting.

**triage.html — rebuilt, 49 cards.** Planets are now in the main **Deep space** group, trailing section gone. Both grounded candidates fold into **Grounded**. Pruned: your 7 from list `-4`, plus bullet-cluster — 8 scenes, all recoverable from git and the archive.

The reason Andromeda "wasn't there": the card existed and pointed at the right path, but thumbnails keep their filenames, so your browser served its cached copy of the old blobby render. All 68 image URLs now carry `?v=<mtime>`, so re-renders show on reload.

**I held `spatial_m31_andromeda` back from the prune** — it was on list `-4`, but you marked it at 23:02 against the old render, and the Hubble-mosaic rebuild only landed at 01:10. Pruning also writes to `pruned_scenes.json`, which permanently blocks regeneration, so I wasn't willing to do that to the thing you'd just asked to see. It's on the page with fresh pixels; tell me if you still want it gone.

Two notes: the ComfyUI pod is on the **GTX 1070**, not the V100 (Ollama holds that) — fine for this job, but the scripts' docstrings claim V100. And `add_planets_to_triage.py` is now dead code, superseded by the generator.

This session is long and expensive at this point. Once you've looked at the new planet cards, `/handoff` and a fresh start would be the efficient move — the remaining threads (Death Valley's unsolved vertical mapping, the Bontecou remap, whether the ring-shadow bake is worth saving) are all clean starting points.

import numpy as np
def Rx(d):
    a=np.radians(d); return np.array([[1,0,0],[0,np.cos(a),-np.sin(a)],[0,np.sin(a),np.cos(a)]])
def Ry(d):
    a=np.radians(d); return np.array([[np.cos(a),0,np.sin(a)],[0,1,0],[-np.sin(a),0,np.cos(a)]])

n_local = np.array([0,0,1.0])                 # annulus lies in local XY
N = Rx(-90) @ (Ry(26.7) @ n_local)            # root conversion  x  ring tilt
N = N/np.linalg.norm(N)
print(f"ring normal in RealityKit frame: ({N[0]:+.4f}, {N[1]:+.4f}, {N[2]:+.4f})")
print(f"  note N_z = {N[2]:+.4f} -> ring brightness is INDEPENDENT of the sun's depth\n")

def report(label, v):
    L=np.array(v,float); L/=np.linalg.norm(L)
    d=float(N@L)
    el=np.degrees(np.arcsin(abs(d)))
    print(f"{label:34s} L=({L[0]:+.3f},{L[1]:+.3f},{L[2]:+.3f})  N.L={d:+.4f}"
          f"  sun {el:5.1f} deg above ring plane"
          f"{'   << EXCEEDS the 26.7 deg physical max' if el>26.8 else ''}")

report("OLD (up-left, shipped)",       (-1.0, 0.45, 0.55))
report("my first fix (0.40,0.10,1.0)", (0.40, 0.10, 1.00))
# Physical max with the largest possible +Z (behind viewer): min-norm solution in the xy plane.
target = np.sin(np.radians(26.7))
xy = target * N[:2]/np.dot(N[:2],N[:2])
Lz = np.sqrt(max(0.0, 1-xy@xy))
best = np.array([xy[0], xy[1], Lz])
report("OPTIMAL behind-viewer+right",  best)
print(f"\n  optimal = ({best[0]:.4f}, {best[1]:.4f}, {best[2]:.4f})")
print(f"  {np.degrees(np.arccos(best[2])):.1f} deg off the view axis;"
      f" azimuth {np.degrees(np.arctan2(best[0],best[2])):.1f} deg right,"
      f" elevation {np.degrees(np.arcsin(best[1])):.1f} deg up")
print(f"  Blender-frame equivalent (X,-Z,Y) = ({best[0]:.4f}, {-best[2]:.4f}, {best[1]:.4f})")

Capture everything a fresh session needs to continue this work, so the current
session can be ended without losing ground.

**Why this exists.** Every turn re-reads the entire accumulated prefix, so cost
per turn climbs with session length — measured at ~26K cache-read tokens per
turn in short sessions versus ~109K past 100 turns. Ending a long session at a
clean boundary and restarting with a handoff is the largest available
efficiency lever. The handoff is what makes ending cheap.

## Where to write it

```
~/.claude/handoffs/<cwd-with-slashes-as-dashes>.md
```

For example, `/Users/rashford/Developer/kitsune` →
`~/.claude/handoffs/-Users-rashford-Developer-kitsune.md`

Overwrite any existing file for this directory — the newest handoff wins. The
`SessionStart` hook loads it automatically in the next session, so **do not**
paste the contents back into chat.

## What to write

Aim for something a competent stranger could act on. Be concrete: real paths,
real command names, real decisions. Skip anything reconstructible from the repo
or from `git log` — those are already available to the next session.

```markdown
# Handoff — <one-line description of the work>
Written: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · Session: <turns> turns

## Where things stand
Two or three sentences. What was being worked on and what state it is in
right now — not a history of the session.

## Decisions made (and why)
Only decisions that would otherwise be re-litigated. Include the reasoning,
because the reasoning is the part that gets lost.

Explicit. If tests ran, say so and give the result. If something was assumed
and never checked, say that too — this is the section that prevents the next
session from building on sand.

The single next action, stated concretely. Then anything queued behind it.

## Open questions
Things the user needs to decide, or that were left unresolved.
```

rings lie in its equatorial plane, so the sun can never be more than 26.7° above them:
**|N·L| ≤ sin(26.7°) = 0.449 is physics, not taste.** Because N_z is exactly 0, ring
brightness is **independent of the sun's depth**, so Rick's requested "behind the viewer,
a bit right" was free. This vector is the minimum-norm solution reaching 0.449 exactly
while maximising +Z: 26.7° off the view axis, 12.7° right, 23.7° up. An earlier attempt at
`(0.40, 0.10, 1.0)` reached only 0.249. Anything above 0.449 is a sun Saturn doesn't have.

**`unlit` no longer suppresses the sun.** The baked globe sets `diffuseColor = (0,0,0)`, so
it has no diffuse response and the feared "second contradictory terminator" is impossible.
All the suppression achieved was leaving the rings black. Every body now gets the sun; the
only thing a light can add to the baked globe is a weak specular (0.5 at roughness 0.9).

**Accepted cost: the ring-shadow bake no longer reads.** With the sun behind the viewer the
ring shadow falls behind the rings. The bake is intact, just not visible from this angle.
The two Saturn cards will therefore look alike again, for a *new* reason. Rick knows.

**Planet previews are composited outside Blender.** `render_preview` now writes RGBA PNG
(`film_transparent = True`; the world colour still lights the scene so ambient is
unchanged) plus a `<name>.cam.json` sidecar carrying the real lens/sensor/resolution.
`scripts/composite_planet_previews.py` then does a proper **gnomonic** reprojection of the
star map — a flat crop of an equirect is not perspective-correct and warps a dense star
field. Decoupled so yaw can be re-chosen without another Cycles run (~7s/body anyway).
Yaws are fixed per body (0/72/144/216/288°) so a re-render changes the body, not the sky.

**`m31_andromeda` was deliberately NOT pruned.** It was on `~/Downloads/triage_removed-4.txt`,
but Rick marked it at 23:02 against the *old blobby* render; the Hubble-mosaic rebuild only
landed at 01:10, and in the same breath he asked to see the new render. `prune_scenes.py`
also writes to `pruned_scenes.json`, which permanently blocks regeneration. Held it and
told him; he has not overridden.

**Why the new Andromeda render "wasn't showing":** thumbnails keep their filenames, so the
browser served its cached copy. `make_triage_page.py` now appends `?v=<mtime>` to every
image URL. This was a caching bug, not a missing card.
